standard_prerequisites.name: The degree of a dominant morphism between integral schemes of equal dimension, and multiplicativity of degrees
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, label lemma-equal-dimension (proof line 1944, claimed as S14-algebra-equal-dimension); Morphisms, label morphisms-lemma-degree-composition (proof line 1951)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first makes the degree of the induced morphisms on the images available, and the second gives the multiplicativity of degrees used to compare the two products.

core_obligations: Reduce to an integral class: take an integral closed subscheme of the source of the relevant dimension, form the images under the two morphisms, which are integral closed subschemes because the morphisms are proper, and reduce to proving the identity for its class (proof lines 1931-1936).
Dispose of the case where the final image has smaller dimension, where both sides vanish (proof line 1937).

Conclude in the equal dimension case: the two induced morphisms satisfy the hypotheses of the equal dimension statement, so the two sides become products of degrees, which agree by multiplicativity of degrees (proof lines 1938-1952).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to an integral class and its images (proof lines 1931-1936).
Vanishing in the smaller dimension case (proof line 1937).
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that proper pushforward is compatible with composition, on cycle classes (statement lines 1923-1929, tag 02R0-adjacent). The proof reduces to an integral class, forms its images under the two proper morphisms, splits off the case where the final image has smaller dimension and both sides vanish, and in the remaining case computes both sides as products of degrees of the induced morphisms and compares them by multiplicativity of degrees. The degree computation is the substance, so the claim is H2.
